_note: C-016: after some weighed judgements, someone affected pushes back, and the player answers. Every answer gets a reply; none is marked right (OPEN-001). Rules in src/domain/pushbacks.ts.

pushbacks.speaker: forest-naturalist
pushbacks.heading: Elian stops you on the bridge

byValue.ribbon: Elian taps one of your ribbons. 'Keep to the stones. So now the trail says boots wear the green away. We counted four pegs on one trail. The edges could dry faster. Walkers could pick bare ground. Your ribbon turns a lead into a cause, and every walker who reads it will believe it.'
byValue.mark: Elian frowns at the two small ties. 'You found fewer green squares by the path, twice, and you put up nothing a walker will read. If boots are doing it, the moss pays while we wait for a second trail. Being careful has a cost too, and the moss is the one paying it.'

answers.reply: Elian listens to the end. 'All right. You weighed it and you can say what you weighed. Write that on the sheet, so the next group knows it was a choice and not a finding.'
Elian nods slowly. 'Changing your mind because someone pushed is not always wisdom. Changing it because you heard a reason you had missed is. Which was it?'

answers.text: Ask what would change Elian's mind
answers.reply: 'A second trail,' Elian says at once. 'Four more pegs where nobody walks the edge. If the edges are still bare there, it is not the boots. Help me set them, and we will both have to accept what they show.'

pushbacks.speaker: sea-harbourkeeper
pushbacks.heading: A skiff crew at the chart wall

byValue.shore: Sora brings over a skiff crew in wet boots. Their steerer points at the chart. 'The shore plan is first and big, and the shoal is a little box in the corner. We have steered by the old chart for twenty years. A reader skims the big one. Put the danger where the eye goes first.'
byValue.water: Sora brings over a skiff crew in wet boots. Their steerer points at the two charts. 'Two charts side by side, and neither says which to trust at low water. We have steered by the old chart for twenty years. Now you make us choose on the quay, with the tide going out.'

answers.text: Keep the wall as it is, and say why
answers.reply: The steerer folds their arms, then nods. 'You thought about it. Fine. Put one line under it that says who should read which chart. We will tell the others.'

answers.text: Change the wall for the crews
answers.reply: Sora watches you move the sheets. 'The first readers we asked were people on dry land. These are the people who will be on the water. That is a reason to change.'

answers.text: Ask what the old chart taught them
answers.reply: The steerer laughs. 'That the old chart is wrong at the north end, and we all know where. It is not on any paper. Write that down, and you have a better chart than either of these.'

byValue.fields: Clerk Sena comes up the bank, and the lower channel crew follow. Their leader speaks first. 'Seven to the rows, three to us. The rows stay green, and our seed beds dry out first. Nobody on the council works the lower channel. Did anyone ask what three buckets means down here?'
byValue.split: Clerk Sena comes up the bank, and both crews follow. 'Five and five,' says the row crew's leader. 'Fair on paper. But now both crews are short, and nobody has enough to do the work properly. Fair can also mean that everybody loses a little, and nobody wins anything.'
byValue.channel: Clerk Sena comes up the bank, and the row crew follow. Their leader speaks first. 'Seven to the channel so it can keep two in reserve. Reserve for what? Our rows need that water this week, not some week that may never come.'

answers.text: Keep the order, and say why
answers.reply: The crew leader listens. 'I still do not like it. But you said who loses, out loud, and you wrote it down. That is more than the last council did.'
Sena raises a hand. 'Careful. If the order changes every time one crew pushes, the loudest crew wins. Change it for a reason, and write the reason next to the change.'

answers.text: Ask what they would need to accept it
answers.reply: The crew leader thinks. 'A date. Tell us when the order will be looked at again, and who will measure our side. Then we can live with it until then.'

pushbacks.speaker: coast-signalkeeper
pushbacks.heading: A crew that acted on the first notice

byValue.true: Signalkeeper Ruan brings a boat crew to the notice board. 'We read the first notice and pulled the boats up at dawn,' says one of them. 'A whole morning lost. Now you change the notice. Next time, how do we know which notice to believe?'

answers.reply: The crew member listens. 'So the first notice was right for what you knew then. I can live with that, if the notice always says when it was written and what it was based on.'

answers.text: Promise not to change notices so fast
answers.reply: Ruan shakes their head. 'Then the next notice will stay wrong for longer. A notice that never changes is not more trustworthy. It is only more stubborn.'

answers.text: Ask what would help them trust a change
answers.reply: 'Tell us how sure you are,' says the crew member. 'Not just the warning. If it says "likely", we pull up half. If it says "certain", we pull up all.'
